subject: Request: RTO/RPO carveout & liability for multi-region failover - BrightBank
messages:
From: Sam Barlow <sam.barlow@brightbank.com>

Cc: BrightBank Security <security@brightbank.com>; Claire Dawson <claire.dawson@brightbank.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Jun 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Multi-region failover - RTO/RPO carveout request

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for yesterday's call. BrightBank is very interested in moving forward, but procurement and security have flagged the multi-region failover wording in the draft SLA. In particular:

- We need a guaranteed RTO of 60 minutes for active region failure and an RPO of 15 minutes for our primary payment workloads.
- We also need a commitment around cross-region data replication windows and a clearly stated standby activation lead time.
- Procurement is asking for a liability cap exception if the RTO/RPO are not met (their legal team wants to carve-in a higher cap tied to unplanned failovers).

Ive attached our redlines (BrightBank_SLA_redlines_v3.pdf) and the security team will follow up with an evidence list. Can you confirm what exceptions Redwood can accept (if any) and what mitigations you can offer?

Wed like a brief written proposal by Thursday so our board counsel can review.

Cheers,
Sam
Sam Barlow
Head of Procurement, BrightBank

Sam — thanks for sending the redlines and flags, appreciated. High level responses below; internal teams are looped for detail and risk assessment.

Quick answers:
- RTO 60m / RPO 15m is aggressive for our current standard hosted+dedicated blend. We can support conditional SLAs with a higher-tier dedicated configuration, plus warm-standby windows, but would need to scope activation cadence and warm cache behavior.
- Liability cap carve-ins are a legal/finance ask — Markus is on copy to advise on exceptions vs our standard cap.
- We can offer additional observability (tracing + activation runbook access) and a post-incident credits multiplier for multi-region activation events as a compromise.

Please expect a short formal proposal from us by Thursday EOD.

Attachments: none (please refer to your attachment).

Regards,

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 19 Jun 2029 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-region failover - RTO/RPO carveout request

Naomi / Markus — internal tech assessment below. Quoting Sam's ask for context:

> - RTO 60 minutes for active region failure
> - RPO 15 minutes for primary payment workloads

Technical notes and constraints:
- The RPO 15m is feasible only if we enable continuous cross-region replication (CRR) with a small buffer window; that requires dedicated bandwidth and can increase cost ~12-18% for the customer's reserved pool.
- RTO 60m depends on: DNS failover TTLs, customer-side reconnection behavior, KV cache warmup, and whether failover uses cold vs warm standby. Our warm standby with pre-warmed model KV caches typically achieves 20-45m depending on sequence-length distribution; cold spin-up can be multiple hours.
- For payment workloads we recommend: dedicated capacity in two AZs in primary region + warm standby in secondary region, KV snapshot sync every 5-10 minutes, and a short-lived prefix cache that rehydrates quickly for common prompts.

Suggested proposal items (to be put in customer-facing doc):
1) Offer conditional RTO 60m / RPO 15m if BrightBank commits to dedicated dual-region reserved capacity and accepts an incremental resilience surcharge.
2) If they cannot commit, offer a best-effort RTO 120m / RPO 30m for hosted with an agreed activation playbook and post-failover validation windows.
3) Provide runbook access, automated failover reports, and a 3x credits multiplier for any activation where we miss the committed SLO.

Ill prepare a short appendix (INF-3456) showing empirical latency/rehydration numbers.

—Karthik
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Jun 2029 10:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-region failover - RTO/RPO carveout request

Team — legal take. Key points to consider before proposing exceptions:

- Liability: our global standard cap is 12 months of fees or $5M (whichever is lower). Increasing the cap for a single customer sets a precedent; if we make a carve-in we should tie it to explicit customer commitments (reserved spend threshold, dedicated architecture, strict incident classification).
- Redlines: BrightBank's redline on page 4 attempts to remove the force majeure language around large-scale regional outages; we should resist broad removal but can clarify activation thresholds.
- Auditability: security will ask for runbook access, audit logs, and SOC2 evidence. We should offer a controlled read-only playbook with a Data Use Agreement and limited retention.

Proposed legal-friendly compromise:
1) Conditional SLA with a 2-tier cap: for documented failures that meet activation criteria, cap at 24 months of fees; for failures caused by negligence/third-party infra, we remain at standard cap.
2) Require a 12-month reserved commitment at >= $200k/month or equivalent monthly committed usage to unlock the conditional cap.
3) Append an explicit failover activation checklist (log + monitoring proof) to avoid ambiguous claims.

If Naomi agrees, I can draft the specific redline language for the contract.

-Markus
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Multi-region failover - RTO/RPO carveout request

Sam — attaching our formal proposal and an appendix summarizing tech tradeoffs (Redwood_DR-appendix.xlsx). Key points: 

1) Conditional SLA offer
- We can accept a committed RTO=60 minutes and RPO=15 minutes for payment workloads under the following conditions: dedicated dual-region reserved capacity, continuous cross-region replication, and a 12-month minimum commitment at $225k/month (or equivalent committed usage).

2) Financial terms & liability
- For activations that meet the documented failover activation checklist, we will increase the liability cap to 24 months of fees (conditional cap). For events outside activation criteria (third-party infra, force majeure as defined), standard cap applies.

3) Operational mitigations
- We will provide read-only runbook access, weekly replication reports for the first 90 days after go-live, and a 3x credits multiplier if the SLA is missed for a qualifying activation.

4) Next steps
- If BrightBank approves, ask procurement/legal to return a single consolidated redline with any targeted language changes. Once agreed we will issue a DocuSign package. Link to draft: https://docusign.com/assembly/1234-ABCD

Attachments: Redwood_DR-appendix.xlsx; proposed redlines to be added to DocuSign.

Thanks — would you be able to route the consolidated redline back by Monday so we can get legal to finalize?

Best,
Naomi Feldman
VP, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
